## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

This PR aims to allow more intentional `HomeAssistantError`s with readable error messages to be raised:

 - Reduce explicit handling of errors, instead opting to allow wrapped `HomeAssistantError`s to propagate.
 - Use a helper function to write attributes, which validates write statuses automatically and similarly raises a `HomeAssistantError` when a failure is encountered.
 - This PR also removes stale `isinstance...Exception` checks, since codepaths to return exceptions as objects are no longer present in ZHA.

issue_context.title: "continue_on_error: true" not working with failed ZHA light.turn_on call
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have two IKEA ZigBee bulbs in a ZHA light group which occasionally throw errors in response to the light.turn_on and light.turn_off commands (typically after a recent ZigBee mesh reorganisation). They are connected to HA via ZHA + a ConBee II.

This report is _not_ about the errors the bulbs sometimes throw - _it's about the fact that these errors are causing scripts to fail, despite using the "continue_on_error: true" setting on the relevant service calls_ (and, in fact, on every single command in the relevant scripts - it's important these scripts complete as many steps as possible, even if some parts fail).

Attached is the relevant script code snippet which produces the script failure when the bulbs throw an error, and logs for the script failure itself.

If any further information is required, let me know and happy to provide it.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.8.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Script / ZHA

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/script

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
[Redacted script name]:
  sequence:
  ...
  - parallel:
    - service: light.turn_on
      data:
        brightness_pct: 1
        color_temp: 153
      target:
        entity_id: light.[Redacted - a ZHA light group]
      continue_on_error: true
    continue_on_error: true
    ...
```

Retrying is now enabled for many more types of commands (some code was directly accessing the zigpy cluster instead of going through the ZHA proxy) so the number of sent requests will be higher in failure cases.
Can this actually raise `KeyError` or should it be moved to after the try/catch?

Sorry, it seems my comment never got posted!

This can raise a `KeyError` in two circumstances:

1. If a device decides to respond with the wrong ID (e.g. you read 0x1234, the device says "0x5678 doesn't exist").
2. If we have no definition for an attribute.
